newsitem.title: UK: BoE's Davies demands TARGET access for EMU "outs".
newsitem.headline: BoE's Davies demands TARGET access for EMU "outs".

text.p: Bank of England deputy governor Howard Davies said on Monday there was no reason why European Union nations outside a single currency could not link into the TARGET settlements system on an equal basis.

"We can see no reason why "out" central banks should not be able to link to TARGET on the same terms as those which apply to the ins," Davies told a European Financial Management and Marketing Association conference in Brussels.
But he said the Bank accepted the need for rigorous policing to stop spillover of intraday credit into the overnight market. "That policing can be achieved through penal interest rates."
"But we can see no monetary policy issue in relation to intraday credit," Davies said.

He said denying fair and equal access to TARGET, which represents the inter-linking of real-time gross settlements systems across Europe, would negate one of its main objectives -- to reduce risks in the banking system.
"Banks would find other ways round the restriction would be more risky. So central banks across Europe will have scored and own-goal," Davies said.
